title: One Machinery, Many Projects
eyebrow: The shared home is real and the first half has landed: the craft definitions now exist once, for every project.

content.label: Where it stands today
content.lead: The shared home exists, both projects are registered against it, and the half that was costing you tokens has landed.

rows: The craft definitions, the shared skills, the typed commands, the voice you are written to
Landed, all of them. Fourteen shared items, one copy each; the racing project keeps only what is about cars, tracks, trees, materials and the renderer.
Two of the racing project's habits that turned out to be craft

The way an image is read for facts rather than recognised, and the way a result is judged against a reference by overlaying them rather than by a single number. Both now belong to every project — a screen is judged the same way a render is.
The pair of eyes any project can send off to look at a screen
Landed, and now named in the worker's own instructions — see below.
Each project's own declaration — its prefix, its systems, how a change proves itself
Landed. Both are written and both check out clean.
The board tools and the session gates

No copy is left. The board tools are reached through a single link to the shared home — the directory is gone — and the shared gates are links too. Two real files remain, held only because another session has unlanded work inside them.
A card filed from the beads checkout landing on the beads board, with nothing pointed anywhere by hand
Done and shown, not assumed — the tool offered that project's own list of systems and the card it wrote is on that board.

blocks.label: The thing you pointed at
blocks.text: A worker was never told to send the looking out, so it did the looking itself and filled up on pictures. Both the worker's and the lead's instructions now name the helpers by hand — the eyes for anything a person would see, the locator for a search, the researcher for how something really behaves, the project's own prover for a measurement — and the lead is told to repeat that in every brief it writes.

blocks.label: Four faults found in the shared tools on the way
blocks.text: Its own suite was red and nobody had run it against a project. The standards answer for one project at a time and every gate the run exercises switched them to whichever checkout it was judging, so later cases were graded against the wrong project's spelling and refused lines that were in fact correct; one refusal was written to a path only the racing project has; one refusal the gates count had no row in the report that spends them; and filing a loose fault was broken outright for every project — anything that got past the wording checks died on the way to the board, and the checks themselves stop above the point where it broke, so nothing caught it. All four fixed, the suite is green against each project in turn, and the last one is held by a case proved by re-breaking it in a scratch copy.

content.label: What you get
content.lead: Any project of yours runs the way the racing one runs — same ticket quality, same gates, same run of steps, same pages — without borrowing anything.

items: An agent filing a beads fault tomorrow lands it on the beads board with nobody watching — the routing is the machinery's, not a habit.
A commit in any project names that project's own cards and is accepted by that project's own gate.
An improvement to the machinery lands once and every project has it the same day.
A new project joins by writing one short declaration, not by copying tools.

A shared pair of eyes: any project can send off a helper that drives the app in a real browser, looks at the screen and reports back in words — the pictures die with it instead of filling up the agent that asked.
The voice you are written to is the house voice now, not this project's private habit: any project of yours answers you the same way.
Proved on a second project already — the beads app answers you in that voice today, keeping no copy of it.

blocks.label: Three things this absorbs
blocks.text: The card about the beads checkout borrowing the pour tools with an overridden address, and the card about the commit gate only recognising its home board's ids, are both closed into this job. The third part of your move instruction — future agents filing beads work on the beads board without being told — is carried here too, so the move job keeps only the split and the move.

content.label: The line: what is shared, what stays a project's own
content.lead: Shared is everything that makes work honest and argues the same way everywhere. A project keeps exactly the five things that differ by subject.

Its board and its card prefix
The gates: what refuses a bad close, a silent question, a commit with no card
Its vocabulary of subjects, in its own words
The run of steps a job walks, and the review by someone who did not write it

blocks.label: Why the line sits there
blocks.text: Each item on the right is exactly what the inventory found hard-wired into the tools today — the racing project's list of subjects, the place its finished work lands, its own name inside the reviewer's introduction, its build traps. Those are the very lines that stop the machinery travelling; pulled into a declaration, everything else moves unchanged.

content.label: How it stays one machinery
content.lead: One live home, run in place; a copy inside a project is refused by a check, the same way report tools already are.

items: The machinery's own test run comes back green from the shared home against every project's declaration — a project with a stale declaration is refused by name, not silently mis-served.
Nothing is versioned per project, so there is no drift to reconcile.
The reporting tools already live this way and stay exactly where they are; this job does not touch them.

content.label: What keeps standing while it moves
content.lead: Both running builds finish their current piece untouched; the switch happens between pieces, never under one.

rows: The chat build in the beads project, mid-piece
The machinery lands between its pieces; its files and its cards are not touched.
Every racing-project session, using today's paths
The old paths keep answering through thin forwarders until each session restarts; behaviour is identical either side of the switch.
The move of the 61 beads cards, running alongside
Its agent moves card data only — no gate, no hook, nothing under the chat build — and skips any card a live session holds. This job's routing work never touches card data, so they cannot cross.

decisions.title: The machinery moves to a home of its own and every project runs it in place — never a copy
decisions.why: One live copy is what makes an improvement land everywhere the same day. The report tools already prove the pattern; a copies check makes forking it impossible rather than impolite.

decisions.title: The shared-versus-own line is drawn at the five declared things
decisions.why: Board and prefix, subject vocabulary, proof of change, where finished work lands, specialist helpers. Each is exactly what was found hard-wired today, and each would make the shared core lie if it stayed hard-wired.

decisions.title: Every gate reads the board of the checkout the work lands in, never the session's home
decisions.why: This is the fix that closes the borrowed-address card and the commit-gate card, and it is what routes tomorrow's beads fault to the beads board with nobody watching.

decisions.title: The racing project is unchanged through the switch
decisions.why: Thin forwarders keep every old path answering until sessions restart; its whole test run must come back green from the shared home before anything is removed.

decisions.title: The card move runs alongside, not behind
decisions.why: Your ruling: the move runs now, in parallel, by its own narrow agent — it touches card data only, never a gate or a hook, and skips anything a live session holds. Checked for crossings: none — this job changes tools, that one moves cards, and the beads checkout's commits are not gated today anyway.

decisions.title: Domain guards and specialist helpers stay home
decisions.why: The render checks, the machine's build traps and the car, track and tree researchers are the racing project's subject knowledge, not machinery. The beads project grows its own equivalents — the screen-driving proof is already wired there.

decisions.title: A plan no longer parks the work waiting for you
decisions.why: Your words today. The house voice now says a job opens with a plan you can read and carries on building under it; only a question that is genuinely yours stops the work. Waiting for you to approve what an engineer can decide spends your attention on a word that carries no decision.

decisions.title: A worker is told which helper to send the looking to, by name, in its own instructions
decisions.why: You pointed at workers filling up on pictures. A helper nobody is told to use is a helper nobody uses: the rule had to sit in the worker's own instructions and in every brief written to it, not in a plan.

decisions.title: The definitions moved first, on their own, ahead of the tools
decisions.why: They are the half that was costing you tokens and the half nothing else is holding. The gates cannot follow yet without walking over live work inside two of those files, and that is worth a few hours rather than someone's afternoon.

next.if_nothing: The definitions stay shared and that much is safe, but the racing project keeps running its own older gates, so an improvement to them still has to be made twice.

steps.step: The racing checkout's board tools and gates become pointers at the shared ones, so there is one copy left — held until the live work inside two of those very files lands, which is a few hours, not a decision
The beads checkout pours its own cards and its commits are accepted by its own gate — no borrowed address anywhere
An agent filing a beads fault from either checkout lands it on the beads board — shown by trying it, not by trusting it
